dict.string: The watch app checks whether you were cycling or running just before a blood sugar reading, to mark it as taken outside, and reads the barometer for your altitude. The iPhone app does not use motion data itself; Apple requires this description here because the watch app ships inside it.

Records where a blood sugar reading was taken, so the outside temperature at that moment can be looked up for it afterwards. The lookup sends that coordinate, height and time to Open-Meteo, a free weather service; nothing else leaves your devices.
Reads your workouts, glucose, active energy and weight so they can be charted alongside your insulin doses. Nothing is written back to Health, and nothing leaves your devices.
This app does not write anything to Health. Apple requires this description whenever an app carries the HealthKit entitlement, even for read-only access.
